# Wang et al. (2022), random-forest PTFs for soil hydraulic-model parameters.

## Source

Wang, Y., Zhou, J., Ma, R., Zhu, G., & Zhang, Y. (2022). Development of a New Pedotransfer Function Addressing Limitations in Soil Hydraulic Models and Observations. Water Resources Research, 58, e2021WR031406.

[DOI: 10.1029/2021WR031406](https://doi.org/10.1029/2021WR031406)

## Functions

### `calc_ptf_wang2022_h2`

Estimate six soil hydraulic-model parameters from sand, silt, and clay with the published H2 random forests.

**Status:** `implemented`

**Prediction target:** van Genuchten alpha, n, and m, saturated volumetric water content, saturated hydraulic conductivity, and the source-defined slope parameter SL.

**Models:** $h(\theta)$ — H2 random-forest estimates of van Genuchten alpha, n, and m, saturated water content, and slope parameter SL; $k(h)$ — H2 random-forest estimate of saturated hydraulic conductivity

#### Inputs

| Name | Type | Unit | Domain | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sand` | `number` | % | 0 <= value <= 100; sand, silt, and clay must sum to 100 under the proposed public percent contract. | Sand content by mass. |
| `silt` | `number` | % | 0 <= value <= 100; sand, silt, and clay must sum to 100 under the proposed public percent contract. | Silt content by mass. |
| `clay` | `number` | % | 0 <= value <= 100; sand, silt, and clay must sum to 100 under the proposed public percent contract. | Clay content by mass. |

#### Outputs

| Name | Unit | Domain | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `alpha` | cm⁻¹ | — | van Genuchten inverse pressure-scale parameter. |
| `n` | dimensionless | — | van Genuchten pore-size distribution parameter. |
| `m` | dimensionless | — | van Genuchten retention-curve shape parameter. |
| `theta_s` | cm³ cm⁻³ | — | Saturated volumetric soil water content. |
| `k_sat` | cm day⁻¹ | — | Saturated hydraulic conductivity. |
| `sl` | dimensionless | — | Source-defined soil hydraulic slope parameter. |

!!! note

    The proposed public contract accepts texture in percent and divides each value by 100 before passing predictors to the serialized models.

!!! note

    The serialized models predict log10(alpha), log10(n), log10(m), and log10(Ks); official code applies 10 raised to each prediction. Theta_s and SL are emitted directly.

!!! note

    Predictor order is sand, silt, clay and must be preserved exactly.

!!! warning

    The supplied source describes texture as article percentages but the executable workbook and code use fractions summing to one. This API makes that boundary explicit by accepting percent and dividing by 100.
